# Build: every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T10:39:51.656Z
> Yo, every skin needs a light and dark.

## What to build
Continue build "Every skin ships a light and a dark colour theme (Studio Pro, Executive, Field, Command, Default and any future skin): quick light/dark switch per skin, follow-system option, coverage check fails if a skin lacks either; full API and voice" (every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 10:39):
"Yo, every skin needs a light and dark."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~20 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Yo, every skin needs a light and dark.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note every-skin-ships-a-light-and-a-dark-colour-theme "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

open: No new UI control in this phase: the existing banner theme-switch widget still swaps the app's own pair. A per-skin light/dark toggle in the Skins menu is a follow-up (needs UI Review shots).

Open PR #557 (Studio Pro, Executive, Field, Command skins) must add `colorThemes` to its four skins when it lands after this, or check-skin-modes and schema validation fail. Its themes: studio-pro-slate, executive-ivory, field-day, command-phosphor each need a partner of the other scheme.
Design packages (day/night packages already exist) are not skins and are not covered by the check.
